title: Principal-quotient conditions for a fractional monogenic algebra
statement: Let $R$ be a normal Nagata domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring] [def-weil-pbc-nagata-ring], let $K$ be its fraction field, and let $0\ne x\in K$. Put $S=R[x]\subseteq K$, and assume explicitly that $R$ and $S$ are Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] (these follow from Nagata and finite type). Let $\mathfrak m$ be a maximal ideal of $S$ containing $x$, put $A=S_{\mathfrak m}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], and let $t=x/1\in A$. An associated prime of $A/tA$ means a prime equal to the annihilator of a nonzero class. Then (i) each associated prime is minimal among primes containing $tA$; (ii) $A_{\mathfrak p}$ is regular [def-weil-regular-scheme] for each such associated prime $\mathfrak p$; and (iii) $A/\mathfrak p$ is analytically unramified [def-weil-pbc-analytically-unramified], meaning that its maximal-ideal-adic completion is reduced.

proof.text: Let $I=\ker(R[T]\to S)$, where $T\mapsto x$. We show by induction on degree that $I$ is generated by the linear polynomials $cT-d$ with $c,d\in R$ and $cx=d$ in $K$. The degree-zero case is zero because $R\hookrightarrow K$ is injective. If $g(T)=c_dT^d+\cdots+c_0\in I$ with $d>0$, [lem-weil-pbc-leading-coefficient-times-root-integral] says $c_dx$ is integral over $R$; normality [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring] gives $d_0:=c_dx\in R$. Then $c_dT-d_0\in I$, and $g-(c_dT-d_0)T^{d-1}$ is in $I$ with degree below $d$. Hence $S/xS\cong R[T]/(I,T)\cong R/J$ with $J=\{d_0\in R: d_0=cx\text{ for some }c\in R\}=R\cap xR$. This identifies the quotient map $R\to S/xS$ and its kernel explicitly.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-normal-domain-fractional-principal-quotient-ass] to the nonzero $x$: $R/J$ has no embedded associated primes, and each associated prime $\mathfrak p$ has height one. Under the surjection $S\to S/xS\cong R/J$, the annihilator of a class pulls back from its annihilator in $R/J$; thus the associated primes of $S/xS$ are the inverse images $\mathfrak q$ of those $\mathfrak p$, each minimal over $xS$. Localization at $\mathfrak m$ keeps only $\mathfrak q\subseteq\mathfrak m$ and preserves this property, so $S_{\mathfrak m}/xS_{\mathfrak m}$ has no embedded primes. For one such $\mathfrak q$, put $\mathfrak p=R\cap\mathfrak q$. The Noetherian normal local domain $R_{\mathfrak p}$ has dimension one, hence is a discrete valuation ring by [lem-sc-normal-dim1-dvr]. Since $x\in\mathfrak qS_{\mathfrak q}$, $x$ cannot have negative valuation in $R_{\mathfrak p}$: otherwise $x^{-1}\in\mathfrak pR_{\mathfrak p}\subseteq\mathfrak qS_{\mathfrak q}$, contradicting $1=xx^{-1}\in\mathfrak qS_{\mathfrak q}$. Therefore $x\in R_{\mathfrak p}$, so $S\otimes_RR_{\mathfrak p}=R_{\mathfrak p}[x]=R_{\mathfrak p}$. The prime $\mathfrak q$ extends to a prime of this local ring containing $\mathfrak pR_{\mathfrak p}$, hence exactly its maximal ideal $\mathfrak pR_{\mathfrak p}$; localizing gives $S_{\mathfrak q}=R_{\mathfrak p}$, a regular local ring.

For the same associated prime $\mathfrak q\subseteq\mathfrak m$, the quotient $S/\mathfrak q$ is $R/\mathfrak p$: the map $R\to S/\mathfrak q$ is surjective because $x\in\mathfrak q$, and its kernel is $\mathfrak p=R\cap\mathfrak q$. Thus $(S/\mathfrak q)_{\mathfrak m}\cong(R/\mathfrak p)_{\mathfrak n}$, where $\mathfrak n=R\cap\mathfrak m$. The quotient $R/\mathfrak p$ is Nagata by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-nagata-nagata], and its local ring is Nagata by [lem-weil-pbc-nagata-localization]. It is a Noetherian local domain, so its completion is reduced by [lem-weil-pbc-local-nagata-domain-analytically-unramified].
